plan.title: Treated vs control DE in colon RSEM counts
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 12-sample human colon bulk RNA-seq study profiled as 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, with a gene-level RSEM expected-count matrix (12,000 genes x 13 columns, first column a gene identifier) and a 12x2 metadata table. The research question is which genes differ between treated and control. Three data facts drive the design. (1) The counts are RSEM expected counts summarized into one matrix, and the per-sample genes.results files with effective lengths were not delivered, so the length correction cannot be reconstructed; the model is fit on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and this limitation is stated in the report (isoform-use changes can appear as differential expression). (2) RSEM expected counts are non-integer; DESeq2 rounds them with a warning while edgeR accepts fractional counts natively, so both paths are run and the report states which method saw which values. (3) sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median; per the low-depth policy it is kept, inspected in QC (PCA, sample distances, library size, detected genes), and its influence is quantified by a sensitivity rerun that excludes it, rather than deleted by default. The primary test is the DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, valid at 6 replicates per group; the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test runs as a second method on the same counts, and the intersection of the two gene sets is reported as the high-confidence result per the two-method robustness rule. No enrichment or pathway step is planned because the research question asks only for differentially expressed genes.

DESeq2 Wald test rerun excluding low-depth sample_01

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

If the strandedness of the library is unknown, infer it before the counting step, and before you trust a count table that a counter made with a strand setting. Run an inference on a sample of aligned reads against the annotation, for example the infer_experiment module of RSeQC, and record the result for every sample. A wrong strand setting counts the antisense reads of an overlapping gene, or it drops half of the reads, and the sample structure QC does not show the error.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression.
